stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Coal producing regions.
solution: Brazil's coal deposits lie almost entirely in the far SOUTH of the country, in the southern plateau region. The chief coal-bearing belt runs through the states of Rio Grande do Sul (the Candiota field, inland from the Atlantic coast and close to the Uruguay border) and Santa Catarina (the Criciuma field, near the south-eastern coast), with a smaller extension into southern Parana. Locate this belt south of the Tropic of Capricorn, roughly between 26 degrees S and 32 degrees S and near the Atlantic seaboard. Shade this southern belt with a distinct symbol, write the name 'Coal producing regions' and add the symbol with its meaning to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Rio de Janeiro.
solution: Rio de Janeiro is a large port city on the SOUTH-EASTERN Atlantic coast of Brazil, at about 23 degrees S latitude, that is, just north of the Tropic of Capricorn. It is the capital of the state of Rio de Janeiro, stands on the shores of Guanabara Bay, lies north-east of Sao Paulo and south-west of the mouth of the river Paraiba do Sul. It is the second largest city of Brazil and lies in the country's most densely settled and most urbanised region, the South-East. Mark it with a dot at this point on the south-eastern coast, write the name 'Rio de Janeiro' beside the dot and add the dot symbol for a city to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Thorny shrubs in Brazil.
solution: Thorny shrub vegetation in Brazil is the Caatinga, and it occupies the semi-arid interior (the sertao) of the NORTH-EASTERN part of the country. It lies inland from the north-east coast, roughly between 5 degrees S and 16 degrees S, spreading over the states of Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Alagoas, Piaui and northern Bahia. This is Brazil's driest, most drought-prone region, so the plants here are short, thorny, deciduous shrubs and cacti with deep roots. Shade this north-eastern interior belt with a distinct pattern, write 'Thorny shrubs (Caatinga)' and add the pattern with its meaning to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Equator.
solution: The Equator (0 degree latitude) passes through the NORTHERN part of Brazil. Drawn from west to east across the map, it crosses the states of Amazonas, Roraima, Para and Amapa, passes a little north of the city of Manaus, cuts across the lower course of the river Amazon and leaves the country near Macapa, the capital of Amapa, close to the mouth of the Amazon on the Atlantic coast. Because of it, the greater part of Brazil lies in the Southern Hemisphere while a small northern portion lies in the Northern Hemisphere. Draw this line as a straight east-west line across northern Brazil, label it 'Equator (0 degree)' and add the line symbol to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : River Paraguay.
solution: The river Paraguay rises in the Mato Grosso plateau of WEST-CENTRAL Brazil and flows southward. It drains the Pantanal, the great marshy wetland of the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, and then runs along Brazil's south-western frontier with Bolivia and Paraguay before leaving the country to join the river Parana in the Parana-Paraguay system. So it is to be shown in the south-west of Brazil, well to the west of the Brazilian Highlands and flowing roughly north to south. Draw its course as a line from the Mato Grosso plateau southwards to the south-western border, write 'R. Paraguay' along the line and add the river symbol to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : States with lowest urban population.
solution: The least urbanised states of Brazil, that is those with the lowest proportion of urban population, lie in the NORTH and the NORTH-EAST. Maranhao, on the north-eastern Atlantic coast west of Piaui, has the lowest share of urban population; Piaui, immediately east of it, and Para, the large state of the northern Amazon lowland astride the lower Amazon, are the next lowest. Acre and Rondonia in the far west of the Amazon basin are also poorly urbanised. These are the regions of dense forest, subsistence farming and few large industrial cities, unlike the highly urbanised South-East. Shade these northern and north-eastern states with a distinct pattern, write their names and add the pattern with its meaning to the index.

context: Observe the map of India and answer the following questions.
stem: Name the lake to the far North of India.
solution: Wular Lake. On the map it is the northernmost lake shown within India, lying in the Kashmir valley of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, on the course of the river Jhelum, and to the west of the rivers Indus and Shyok. It is the largest freshwater lake in India.

context: Observe the map of India and answer the following questions.
stem: Name the major west flowing rivers in Central India.
solution: The Narmada and the Tapi (Tapti). Both are shown in central India flowing from east to west, in rift valleys between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, and both empty into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat.

context: Observe the map of India and answer the following questions.
stem: Where does the river Kaveri originate ?
solution: The river Kaveri originates at Talakaveri on the Brahmagiri hills of the Western Ghats, in the Kodagu (Coorg) district of Karnataka. The map marks its source with a dot against the label 'Brahmagiri' in the south-western part of the peninsula. From there the Kaveri flows south-east across the Deccan plateau and drains into the Bay of Bengal.

context: Observe the map of India and answer the following questions.
stem: River Manas is the tributary of which river ?
solution: The river Manas is a tributary of the Brahmaputra. On the map it is shown in the north-east, rising in the Himalayas of Bhutan and flowing southward through Assam to join the Brahmaputra on its northern bank.

context: Observe the map of India and answer the following questions.
solution: The map indicates the drainage of India, that is, its main rivers and lakes. As the index shows, the lines represent the rivers and the dots represent their sources. It therefore shows the courses of the Himalayan rivers such as the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra with their tributaries, the peninsular rivers such as the Narmada, Tapi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, and the important lakes such as Wular, Sambhar, Loner, Chilka, Kolleru, Pulicat and Vembanad, along with the seas that surround the country.
